t.E251.agn: In 2017 EFSA maintained the acceptable daily intake (ADI) at 3.7 mg/kg body weight, expressed as nitrate ion. Nitrate from the additive makes up a small part of total intake; it reported that when natural nitrate in vegetables is also taken into account, the limit may be exceeded in all age groups. IARC classifies ingested nitrite and nitrate under conditions that result in nitrosamine formation in Group 2A.
t.E251.body: Nitrate may be converted to nitrite in the mouth.
t.E251.eff.0.t: It may be converted to nitrite in the mouth; IARC classifies ingested nitrite and nitrate under conditions that result in nitrosamine formation in Group 2A
t.E251.eff.1.t: When natural nitrate in vegetables is also counted, the daily limit may be exceeded; the additive's share is small
t.E251.eval: IARC classifies the intake of nitrite and nitrate under conditions that may lead to nitrosamine formation in the body as Group 2A (probably carcinogenic). It is used in processed meats such as sucuk, sausages and salami to preserve colour and prevent botulism.
t.E251.prod: Mostly obtained from natural deposits (caliche) in Chile by dissolving them in brine and crystallising; it may also be produced chemically.
t.E251.regx.0: Re-evaluated; ADI of 3.7 mg/kg (expressed as nitrate ion) maintained.
t.E251.summary: A nitrate salt; it is converted to nitrite in the body and in meat. It is used in cured meats and some cheeses.
t.E251.what: It is used as a preservative in cured meats; it may be converted to nitrite in the body and within the product.
